GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.4727 
ANSWERED ON 31.03.2022 
  
PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM 
 
4727.     SHRI KANUMURU RAGHU RAMA KRISHNA RAJU: 
 
 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)   whether the Government is implementing Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram 
(PMJVK) across the country with financial outlay of 1390 crores and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b)   the schemes and programmes being implemented under PMJVK along with the 
funds allocated and released to each district in Andhra Pradesh; and 
(c)    the status of the schemes and programmes undertaken till date under PMJVK? 
 
  
A N S W E R 
  
THE MINISTR OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI)  
  
(a) to (c) The Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme, which was restructured and implemented with effect from May, 2018, in 1300 
identified Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs) of the Country with the objective to 
develop socio-economic infrastructure assets and basic amenities in these areas. The 
areas covered under PMJVK were increased from 90 Districts originally, to 308 Districts 
in 33 States/ UTs w.e.f. May, 2018. The MCAs included 870 Minority Concentration 
Blocks (MCBs), 321 Minority Concentration Towns (MCTs) and 109 Minority 
Concentration District Headquarters (MCD Hqrs) added for the first time. The scheme 
has now further been revised for implementation w.e.f from 2022-23 onwards in all 
Districts of the country including all the Aspirational Districts. 

Since the year 2014-15, the Ministry has sanctioned projects worth Rs.18257.89 crores 
under PMJVK. During this period more than  49,000 major projects have been 
sanctioned which includes 38 Degree Colleges, 177 Residential Schools, 1,550 School 
Buildings, 23,094 Additional Class Rooms, 14,312 Teaching Aid & Smart Classrooms, 
691 Hostels, 27 Working Women Hostels, 94 ITI Buildings and additional facilities in 17 
ITIs, 14 Polytechnics, 31 Skill Centres, 2324 Health Projects,01 Medical college, 01 
Unani Medical College, 01 Nursing Hostel and upgradation of Hamidiya Hospital at 
Gandhi Medical College and linked hospitals in Bhopal, 01 Agriculture College, 01 
Medical Hunar Hub project comprising of a 300 bedded hospital, a Nursing College, a 
Paramedical College and a Pharmacy College, a Skill Development Centre alongwith 
hostels with capacity of 2300 and also a 200 bedded Working Women Hostel,  413 
Sadhbhav Mandaps, 01 Sadbhav Kendra, 170 Common Service Centres, 553 Market 
Sheds, 12 Hunar Hubs, 6742 Sanitation/Toilet projects, 91 Sports Facilities including 
Augmentation of Luwangpokpa Cricket Stadium in Manipur and Upgradation of P.A. 
Sangma Outdoor Stadium in Meghalaya, etc. 
 
The budget outlay for the scheme for the current financial year i.e 2021-22 was Rs. 
1390.00 crore which has been increased to Rs. 1650.00 crores for BE 2022-23. During 
2021-22, projects worth Rs. 2230.38crores have been approved under PMJVK. 
 
The areas covered under PMJVK in Andhra Pradesh were increased from 4 Districts 
originally, to 6 Districts covering 07 blocks and 12 towns in May 2018. The scheme after 
further revision for implementation w.e.f from 2022-23 will cover all the districts of Andhra 
Pradesh.Since 2014-15 a total of 2147 projects amounting to Rs. 621.93 crores have 
been approved under PMJVK in the State of Andhra Pradesh. Theprojects approved in 
Andhra Pradesh includes17-Residential Schools, 17-School Buildings, 32-Hostels,108-
Additional Class Rooms (ACRs), 12-Toilets, 01-Library, 1- Degree College, 9-ITIs, 4-
Polytechnics, 1- Additional facility in Polytechnics, 2-Working Women Hostels, 224- 
Anganwadi Centers, 9-Common Service Centres (CSC), 6- Sadbhav Mandaps, 4-Hunar 
Hubs, 1700- Bicycles etc.  
  
The district wise funds allocated and releasedin Andhra Pradesh since 2014-15 is 
available on the website of the Ministry i.e. www.minorityaffairs.gov.in.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.4728 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31st March, 2022 
 
City Gas Distribution Network 
 
4728 SHRIMATI RITA BAHUGUNA JOSHI: 
Will the Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to allocate City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network to all the 
smart cities in the country; 
(b) if so, the timeframe fixed for the same; 
(c) the details of the households having Petroleum Natural Gas (PNG) connection and the details of 
proposed expansion of PNG connections in Uttar Pradesh along with the timeline fixed for the 
purpose; 
(d) whether some of Ujjawal beneficiaries are also getting PNG connection instead of LPG cylinder; 
(e) if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) if not, whether the Government has any proposal to give PNG Connections to the Ujjawal 
beneficiaries in the near future to replace the LPG cylinder and if so, the details thereof; 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
(a) to (c) Establishment of CNG station and providing PNG connection  are a part of development of 
City Gas Distribution (CGD) network and the same is carried out by the entities authorized by the 
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB).  After 11 th CGD Bidding Round, PNGRB 
has authorized / issued Letters of Intent for 289 Geographical Area (GA).  Further under 11 th A CGD 
bidding round, PNGRB has invited bids for 6 GAs covering 28 districts in 6 states / UT.  After the 
completion of 11 th and 11 th A CGD bidding rounds, CGD network shall potentially cover 98% of 
population and 88% of geographical area of the country including smart cities situated within the 
GAs.  As per Minimum Work Programme (MWP) authorized entities have committed to provide   
38,92,142 PNG connections in Uttar Pradesh. As on 31.01.2022, there are 11.35 Lakh PNG 
connections in the State of Uttar Pradesh.  After the 11 th and 11 th A rounds, Uttar Pradesh will be 
fully covered under the CGD network as per the MWP to be fulfilled by the entities in the prescribed 
time limit of 8-10 years from the date of authorization.   
(d) to (f) Pradhan Mantri UjjwalaYojana (PMUY) was launched in May 2016, with an objective to 
make clean cooking fuel such as LPG available to the rural and deprived households which were 
otherwise using traditional cooking fuels such as fire wood, coal, cow dung, etc.  As on 31.01.2022, 
under the PMUY, 9 Crore LPG connections have been given to BPL households.  At present, there is 
no any proposal to give PNG connections in lieu of LPG connections to the Ujjwala beneficiaries.

4729.  DR. G. RANJITH REDDY: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 2300 kilometres of road projects have 
 been identified under Bhar atmala Pariyojna Phase -I in the State of 
 Telangana with an estimated cost of Rs. 56,000 crores; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for awarding only 
 520 kilometres of road projects so far; 
(c) the time by which the remainin g 1800 kilometres are likely to be 
 undertaken ; 
(d) the time frame f ixed for comple tion of Bharatmala Pariyojna in the 
 State of Telangana; and 
(e) whether the works are progress ing as per schedule and if not, the 
 reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to  (e)         2,178 km has been envisaged for development under 
Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase -I with cost of Rs. 54,485 crore in the State 
of Telangana. Works comprising length of 568 km having total cost of Rs. 
9,906 crore have been awarded and length of abo ut 336 km has been 
completed.

various pre-construction activities including land acquisition, clearances 
for utility as also forest and Environment are completed and based on the 
preparedness of the project, the work is awarded.   The pre-construction 
activities i.e. land acquisition, utility shifting as also clearances of Forest 
department are carried out in consultation with various State Governments 
and is a time consuming activity, which has been expedited to minimise 
the delay at the programme level.

27.

†4730. SHRI ASHOK MAHADEORAO NETE:  
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has formulated any plan to bring reforms in the power 
sector in the country;  
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(c)  the quantum of funds proposed to be allocated by the Government for 
implementation of the said plan? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)  :    Government of India ha ve launched the Reforms -based and Results -linked 
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme with the objective of improving the quality and 
reliability of power supply to consumers through a financially sustainable and 
operationally efficient distribution Sector. The scheme has an outlay of Rs.3,03,758 crore

Liquidity Infusion Scheme (LIS); Additional Borrowing of 0.5% of GSD P to States linked to 
power sector reforms; introducing additional prudential norms for lending by Power

4739.  SHRI PRAJWAL REVANNA 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has approved national pr oject status to Upper Bhadra lift irrigation projec t 
in the State of Karnataka and if so, the details th ereof along with funds sanctioned and utilised by t he 
Government till date; 
(b) whether the DPR of the project has been cleared  by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate  
Change and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the details of funding pattern for the national irrigation projects including Upper Bhadra Project? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI   
 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
 
(a) For inclusion of a project for funding under Nation al Projects (NP) scheme of this Ministry, it is 
required to be first appraised by Central Water Com mission (CWC), and accepted by the Advisory 
Committee on Irrigation, Flood Control and Multipur pose Projects of this Ministry. Thereafter, 
investment clearance is required to be obtained by the State Government. Subsequently, if the project 
meets the laid down norms for the NP scheme, it is required to be considered by the High Powered 
Steering Committee (HPSC) set up for the purpose. O n being recommended by HPSC, and as per 
availability of funds etc., Government of India may  approve inclusion of a project under the NP 
scheme.  
  
Subsequent to acceptance by Advisory Committee in D ecember, 2020 and grant of investment clearance 
in March, 2021, Upper Bhadra project has been recom mended by HPSC for inclusion under NP scheme, 
in its 14 th  Meeting held in February, 2022. However, its inclu sion under NP scheme shall require 
specific approval of Government of India.  
  
Central assistance for the project shall be availab le only once the project is included under the NP 
scheme.  
  
(b)  Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change ha s accorded environmental clearance for Upper 
Bhadra Project vide letters dated 05.01.2010 and 10.07.2017.  
  

  
(c)  As per the latest Guidelines of NP scheme published  in 2022, the funding pattern under the NP 
scheme is as below:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.4740 
ANSWERED ON 31.03.2022 
 
SEEKHO AUR KAMAO SCHEME 
4740. SHRI JAYADEV GALLA. 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
a) the details of the number of minority youths trained under the Seekho Aur 
Kamao scheme, state, category and district-wise including for Andhra 
Pradesh; 
b) the details of the number of trainees who were employed within three months 
of being trained, state and gender-wise; and 
c) the details of the number of trainees who are currently unemployed, state and 
gender-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI) 
a) to c) ‘Seekho Aur Kamao’ scheme (Learn and Earn) is a placement-linked skill 
development scheme for minorities. It aims to upgrade the skills of minority youth (in 
the age group of 14-45 years) in various modern/ traditional skills depending upon 
their qualification, present economic trends, and market potential, that can earn them 
suitable employment or make them suitably skilled to take up self-employment. 33% 
of the total targets in the scheme are earmarked for female beneficiaries. 
 
Under Seekho aur Kamao scheme, till date about 4.60 lakh beneficiaries have been 
trained under the same and of this, 2.64 lakh beneficiaries (58% of total trained) are 
females.    In the state of Andhra Pradesh, 14,845 No. of beneficiaries have been 
trained out of which 8,951 are female beneficiaries.   
 
The scheme is implemented by Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) that are 
empanelled by the Ministry by inviting applications from all over India. The scheme 

mandates at least 75% placement out of which at least 50% should be in wage 
employment. The data on number of trainees who were trained and employed within 
three months of being trained is not maintained in the Ministry. However, 1,72,005 
beneficiaries have been reported as placed/ employed out of which 7,577 are in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh.    
Beside this, the Ministry also implements  “Nai Manzil”  Scheme to benefit the 
minority youth  (both men & women) belonging to six notified minority communities of 
17-35 years of age,  who do not have  formal school leaving certificate, i.e., those in 
the category of school –dropouts  or  these educated in community education 
institutions like Madarasas. 30% of the beneficiary seats are earmarked for 
girl/women candidates and 5% of the beneficiary seats for persons with disability 
belonging to the minority community under the scheme.  The scheme provides a 
combination of formal education (Class VIII or X) and skills, to enable beneficiaries to 
seek better employment and livelihood.  The Scheme is implemented through 
selected Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) which are empanelled through an 
open transparent process by inviting Expression of Interest (EOIs) for organizations.  
Under the Nai Manzil scheme, since inception, a total of 98697 beneficiaries (both 
male and female) were  enrolled out of which 39,635 female candidates were skill 
certified.  Out of the total placement of 34,340 beneficiaries, 833 are in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh. 
Maulana Azad Education Foundation (MAEF) has launched Gharib Nawaz Skill 
Development Training for minorities from the year 2017-18 which has been renamed 
as Gharib Nawaz Employment Scheme from the year 2019- 20. Under this scheme 
various short-term job oriented skill development courses are provided to minorities 
youth in order to enable them for skill based employment. This scheme is being 
implemented as per common norms of the Ministry of Skill Development & 
Entrepreneurship (MSD&E) through the empanelled Program Implementing Agencies 
(PIAs). Under this Scheme, since inception a total 67,986 beneficiaries ( out of which 
39,297 females) have been skill trained .  
Upgrading the Skills and Training in Traditional Arts/Crafts for Development 
(USTTAD) scheme was launched on 14th May, 2015 to preserve the rich heritage of 
traditional arts/crafts of minorities. The scheme aims at capacity building and 
updating the traditional skills of master craftsmen/artisans, documentation of 
identified traditional arts/crafts of minorities, set standards for traditional skills, training 
of minority youths in various identified traditional arts/crafts through master craftsmen, 
and develop national and international market linkages. The scheme is implemented 
through Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs). A total of 23,130 trainees (out of 
which 20620 females ) have been trained under the USTTAD Scheme so far.

NO. 4742.  SHRI SAUMITRA KHAN:  
SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)   whether the Government has any proposal aimed at me eting housing 
needs of people living in urban areas and if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether the Government has any data regarding the number of 
projects executed under various housing schemes, St ate-wise 
including West Bengal and Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof, 
district-wise;  
(c)  whether cities selected under Swachh Surveksha n are being 
provided with financial incentives and if so, the p arameters used to 
select the cities under the scheme along with the b enefits that the 
selected cities would get thereunder;  
(d)  the rankings of various cities of West Bengal and Rajasthan under 
Swachh Survekshan; and 
(e)  whether the Government has any specific plans for urban housing in 
Bankura, Jaipur and Ajmer and if so, the details thereof? 
           ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
 MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a)  & (b):  Land and Colonization are State subjects. T herefore, schemes 
related to housing for people living in urban area are being implemented by 
State/ Union Territories (UTs). Data related to hou sing schemes of States/ 
UTs is not maintained by this Ministry. However, Mi nistry of Housing and 
Urban   Affairs  is  supplementing    the  efforts  of  State/ UTs  by   providing 
 
...2/- 
 
 

-2- 
 
Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana  – Urban (PMAY-U) 
since 25.06.2015 for construction of houses for all  eligible families/ 
beneficiaries. Eligible beneficiaries can avail the  benefit of PMAY-U through 
any one of the available four verticals i.e., Benef iciary-led Construction 
(BLC), Affordable House in Partnership (AHP), In-Si tu Slum Redevelopment 
(ISSR) and Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) base d on their preference. 
Based on the project proposals submitted by States/  UTs, more than 115 
lakh houses have been sanctioned across the country , out of which more 
than 95 lakh have been grounded and more than 56 la kh have been 
completed/ delivered to the beneficiaries so far. T he  Scheme Guidelines are 
available at https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guid elines/62381c744c188-
Updated-guidelines-of-PMAY-U.pdf. The State-wise details of houses 
sanctioned, grounded and completed/ delivered under  PMAY-U are at 
Annexure-I. The district-wise details of houses san ctioned, grounded and 
completed/delivered in the States of West Bengal an d Rajasthan under 
PMAY-U are at Annexure-II. 
 
(c): All cities covered under Swachh Bharat Mission  - Urban are expected to 
participate in Swachh Survekshan. No financial ince ntives are provided by 
Government of India for participating; it is part o f Mission’s monitoring 
interventions.  
(d): West Bengal did not take part in Swachh Survek shan 2020 and 2021. 
The major results of Swachh Survekshan 2021 in Raja sthan are at 
Annexure-III.  
e): The details of houses sanctioned under PMAY-U i n Bankura, Jaipur and 
Ajmer are 11,366, 64,965 and 10,090 respectively.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4744 
ANSWERED ON 31.03.2022 
GLOBAL SOLAR GRID  
4744. COL. RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE 
Will the Minister of New and Renewable Energy be please to state: 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
(a)&(b) The Government is conducting a study for developing the long -term vision, implementation 
plan, road map and institutional framework for implementing a global grid named as One Sun One 
World One Grid (OSWOWOG).   
At Glasgow on 02 -11-2021, during COP26, a  One Sun Declaration was issued by India and 88 other 
countries. To help deliver the vision of OSOWOG, it was resolved to combine efforts and create a n 
inter-connected global grid. This will, inter -alia, include building long distance cross -border 
transmission lines to connect renewable energy generators and demand centres across continents. 
(c) The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy has not initiated any research on taking up solar energy 
directly from the atmosphere of the earth.  
(d) India and United Kingdom  have jointly written to USA, Australia, African Union, France, Germany 
and Oman to participate in the Ministerial Steering Group for the global “Green Grids Initiative – One 
Sun One World One Grid”. 
(e) & (f): No, Sir. 
***** 
 
(a) whether the Government is in talks with  other countries towards developing a global solar grid;  
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Government is conducting scientific research and looking into the possibilities of 
taking up solar energy directly from the atmosphere of the earth and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has constituted any international i nter governmental and scientific 
panels to look into the feasibility and possibility of a global solar grid and if so, the details thereof;  
(e) whether the Indian Space Research Organization is collaborating with experts in the renewable 
energy field from India and abroad to conduct studies and innovate in the area of a global solar 
grid; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof?

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION  No. 4745 
ANSWERED ON 31st  MARCH, 2022 
  
ROAD CONNECTIVITY IN NAXAL AFFECTED AREAS 
  
4745.         SHRI RAJA AMARESHWARA NAIK:  
SHRI VINOD KUMAR SONKAR:  
SHRIMATI SANGEETA KUMARI SINGH DEO:  
DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR: 
                   SHRI RAJVEER SINGH (RAJU BHAIYA): 
SHRI BHOLA SINGH: 
DR. JAYANTA KUMAR ROY: 
  
       Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्गमंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has any programme to connect remote and naxal 
affected areas by roads to ensure speedy development of such areas;  
(b) if so, the details of physical and financial progress during the last three years, 
State-wise;  
(c) the details of proposals from States received and approved along with those 
which are pending with the Union Government during the last three years and 
the current year, State-wise including Uttar Pradesh;  
(d) whether the Government is aware of the problems being faced in 
construction/maintenance works in naxal affected areas and if so, the details 
thereof along with reaction of the Government thereto; and  
(e) the remedial steps being taken by the Government to bring remote and naxal 
affected areas into mainstream through road connectivity? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS 
  
(Shri NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) & (b)    Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) has launched Road 
Requirement Plan -I (RRP -I) in 2009 with an objective to improve road 

connectivity in Naxal affected/Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected areas in 9 
States, viz., Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhatisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. A total of 234 works 
involving improvement of 5362 km of roads were sanctioned by this Ministry 
under RRP-I, out of which 210 works of 5038 km length have been co mpleted. 
The details of physical and financial progress of these works during the last 
three years are at Annexure -I. Subsequently, Ministry of Rural Development 
(MoRD) also launched Road Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism 
Affected Areas (RCPLWEA) in the year 2016 to improve the road connectivity in 
44 worst affected LWE districts and some adjoining districts in the above 9 
States, viz. Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh . The scheme has twin 
objectives of ensuring socio -economic development of the area as also 
enabling smooth and seamless anti -LWE operations by the security forces.   A 
total of 10,901.45 km road length has been sanctioned by MoRD and 5,560.74 
km of road le ngth has been completed. The details of physical and financial 
progress during the last three years under RCPLWEA, State wise under MoRD 
are at Annexure - IA. 
  
(c)    No proposal has been received and approved under RRP-I by MoRTH during 
the last three years and the current year as most of the works under RRP-I have 
already been sanctioned. The details of proposals approved and those pending 
under RCPLWE by MoRD during the last 3 years and current year, State-wise are 
at Annexure -II. 
(d) & (e) While implementing the schemes, challenges like availability of 
limited construction hours per day, lack of consistent/adequate deployment of 
security personnel, frequent bandhs/strikes called by naxals, lesser 
participation of bidders in naxal a ffected areas etc., have been faced, which 
had impacted the overall progress of the scheme. Other issues  like delays in 
land acquisition, forest clearance, poor contracting capacity of States, lack of 

response to tenders, law and order issues, financial c apability of States to 
release funds in time, execution capacity of states / State Rural Road 
Development Authorities (SRRDAs), which hindered progress of the scheme are 
also encountered.  Several steps, like delegation of powers to State 
Government authorities to accept bids with higher tender rates compared to 
normal cases, increase in deployment of security personnel to the extent 
feasible, allowing splitting of works to facilitate deployment of more number 
of local contractors etc., have been taken to ex pedite the completion of the 
works as well as to bring remote and naxal affected areas into mainstream 
through road connectivity program. Similarly, other measures like, making 
eligible  the Tribal (Schedule V) areas and selected Tribal / Backward Districts 
/ unconnected habitations in these areas with a population of 250 persons and 
above in the Core Network as per 2001 Census   under Pradhan Mantri Gram 
Sadak Yojna (PMGSY) for connectivity with roads, additional relaxation to 
connect habitations with popul ation of 100 persons and above as per 2001 
census in the critical Left -Wing Extremism affected blocks (as identified by 
Ministry of Home Affairs) have also been taken. T he programme is being 
monitored at regular intervals through Regional Review Meetings ( RRMs), 
Performance Review Committee (PRC) Meetings and Pre -Empowered / 
Empowered Committee Meetings with the States. Necessary hand - holding of 
the state in this regard was done wherever required through Inter -
departmental meetings etc. 
  

 ANNEXURE-I 
  
ANNEXURE- I REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 31ST MARCH, 2022 
ISSUES RELATED TO FLYOVER AT PANIPAT 
4746.  SHRI SANJAY BHATIA: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the flyover in Panipat city had been completed in 2006 
and a private company has collected a sum of 669 crore rupees as 
toll from the toll booths at Panipat; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c)  whether the Government is aware that the residents are facing 
problems of jams, dust and accidents due to the said flyover and the 
commuters have to pay toll even without using the said flyover;  
 
(d)  if so, whether the Government propose to find a solution of the 
said problem immediately; and  
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) & (b)  The provisional completion of project stretch from km 86 to 
km 96 of NH -44 (including flyover in Panipat City) was issued on 
15.07.2008 and Commercial Operation of the project commenced 
since 17.07.2008. The Concessionaire has collected toll fee amount 
of Rs. 688.91 crore till February, 2022 as per Concession Agreement. 
(c)  After construction of Panipat Elevated flyover, traffic on highway 
has eased out. However, unauthorized parking of local commuters’ 

vehicle on service road leads to congestion. The project  stretch is 
from km 86.00 to km 96.00 and, as per Concession Agreement, 
commuters have to pay user fee, when crossing toll plaza. Moreover, 
residences within distance of 20 km from the toll plaza have to pay 
only Rs. 285/- monthly for their private vehicles. 
(d) & (e)  To ease out congestion beneath elevated section, feasibility 
study has been carried out and detailed proposal has been prepared.

MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS 
  
4747.     SHRI THIRUNAVUKKARASAR SU: 
SHRI RAVNEET SINGH BITTU: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a huge increase in the number 
of fake/false motor accident claims in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along the reasons therefor, State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to set up a new portal and 
generate unique number to curb filing of fake or multiple motor accident 
claims in the country; 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the extent to which the new portal is 
likely to check such fake/false claims; 
(e) the time by which it is likely to be introduced; 
(f) the other measures being taken by the Government to curb such 
fake/false claims in the country? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a)  to (b) No such data is maintained. 
  

(c) to (f) The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has issued 
notification GSR 164 (E) dated 25 th February, 2022  to mandate the 
procedure for detailed investigation of road accidents, the Detailed 
Accident Report (DAR) and its reporting, along with timelines for 
different stakeholders, including electronic submission of the details 
on eDAR portal for quick settlements of claims by the Motor Accident 
Claim Tribunal (MACT) as well as to check fake/false motor accident 
claims.

IMPLEMENTATION OF DDUGJY 
 
4748.  SHRI ANURAG SHARMA:  
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the present status of implementation of Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana 
(DDUGJY) in Uttar Pradesh especially in Jhansi and Lalitpur districts;  
 
(b)  whether the Government has achieved the targets fixed under the said yojana;  
 
(c)  if so, the details thereof, year-wise;  
 
(d)  the quantum of funds earmarked, sanctioned and spent under the s aid yojana 
during the said period in Uttar Pradesh; and  
 
(e)  the number of districts/villages targeted to be electrified during the current year, 
particularly in Jhansi and Lalitpur in Uttar Pradesh? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) :    Government of India launched Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana 
(DDUGJY) in December, 2014 for various rural electrification works including separation 
of agriculture and non -agriculture feeders, strengthen ing and augmentation of sub -
transmission & distribution infrastructure, metering at distribution transformers/ 
feeders/consumers and electrification of villages across the country including Uttar 
Pradesh. As reported by the State of Uttar Pradesh, all the inhabited un -electrified 
census villages in the State including districts Jhansi and Lalitpur, stand electrified . The 
works of DDUGJY have been completed in Uttar Pradesh State including Jhansi and 
Lalitpur districts.  Details  of infrastructure created un der DDUGJY in Uttar Pradesh   are 
at Annexure. 
 
There is no upfront allocation of funds for any State/District under DDUGJY 
scheme. Funds are released for sanctioned projects in installments based on the 
reported utilization of the amount released in the pr evious installments and fulfillment of 
stipulated conditionalities. 
Under DDUGJY (including ad ditional infra) projects of Rs. 29,266 cr. 
(including GBS grant of Rs .22238.1 cr.) have been sanctioned. As on 28.02.2022, a grant 
amount of Rs .18,983 Cr . has been  disbursed to the State of Uttar Pradesh and the 
amount has been fully utilized.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4749 
ANSWERED ON 31ST MARCH, 2022 
  
MULTI MODAL LOGISTICS PARK AT JOGIGHOPA 
  
4749.         SHRI ABDUL KHALEQUE: 
  
          Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क  परिवहन  औि  िाजमार्ग  मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a)   the time by which Multi Modal Logistics Park at Jogighopa is 
likely to start functioning; 
(b)   the revenues likely to be generated as a result thereof in the 
three years from start of its operation; 
(c)    the expected employment to be generated as a result thereof in 
the next five years; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to establish an airport at 
Jogighopa as part of Multi Modal Logistics Park; 
(e)    if so, the time by which the airport project is likely to be taken 
up and completed; and 
(f)     if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a)    The Multi Modal Logistics Park at Jogighopa is likely to start 
functioning after completion of the construction work at the site. The 
completion date of construction work at MMLP Jogighopa is 
31.12.2022. 
  

(b)  As per the assessment carried out at project preparation stage, 
revenue of an amount of Rs. 1000 Cr (approx) is estimated in the first 
three years from start of operation. 
  
(c)    As per the Detailed Project Report (DPR), the estimated total 
employment to be generated after commencement of MMLP is about 
11521 people. 
  
(d)    No Sir. 
  
(e)     Does not arise. 
  
(f)   The concept of Multi Modal Logistics Park does not envisage the 
establishment of transport mode itself rather this deals with 
providing connectivity at least from two transport modes.   MMLP 
Jogighopa is being provided connectivi ty from Highway, Railways & 
Inland Waterways.
